acceptance.atomic: Core transaction hook projects registered source inserts, patches, replacements, deletes and record-history restores before commit; index/capacity failures roll back application rows, history and index. Independent pre-opened connections and real child processes use the persisted binding.
acceptance.authority: Scope policy, owner-derived scope and optional current record policy precede ranking; current scoped source version/content/scope must match. Deleted, stale, inaccessible and duplicate candidates cannot supply snippets or consume authorized ranking capacity. Rejected async policies are denied and their promises contained.
acceptance.rebuild: Persistent bounded cursor and generation; concurrent source edits/inserts/deletes remain indexed. Restart and process death preserve the last committed boundary. Exact old repair revision conflicts rather than restarting accepted progress; resume calls do not rewrite source rows.
acceptance.diagnosis: Bounded union scan reports missing/stale/orphan/duplicate ID counts, byte/record inventory and continuation cursor. Does not certify unscanned rows.
acceptance.limits: At most 16 bindings; up to 50000 source records and 64 MiB text bytes per binding, default 16 MiB, plus per-scope and per-record bounds. Final-state swaps accepted; failed rebuild does not advance cursor. Descriptor version/identity and generation fences reject unsupported persistence or stale handles.
acceptance.browser: Actual HTTP/SQLite/auth flow verifies keyboard search/open, retained focus, 390px contained long-title layout, scope change during delayed response, disposal during delayed response and revoked session failure. Automated UI regressions prevent late errors/enabling submit and stale record opens.
acceptance.compatibility: Unlinked applications gain no search tables and preserve an active recovery epoch. Failed first registration rolls back metadata, FTS and shadow tables together. Optional/defaulted source fields are rejected; string literals/enums are supported.

before.scope: Pre-feature manual indexing retains initial content after patch and deletion without an application indexing worker. This demonstrates the automatic projection gap; manual eventual consistency was documented.

initialReleaseFailure.reason: The existing fake element omitted its standard style object. Fixture corrected; two meaningful UI race regressions added; full release gate rerun successfully.

compatibility.default: Existing manual service contract remains available; source-linked services expose server-only rebuild/inspect/detach and cannot manually forge entries. Browser HTTP search remains compatible.
compatibility.migration: First source registration transaction adds versioned binding metadata, FTS and shadow tables; source rows are untouched. Unlinked application schemas are unchanged. Registration on a sealed recovery database is refused. Previously used source_search_ application names must be renamed/migrated before upgrading.
compatibility.rollback: Drain writers, unmount search, fenced detach with upgraded service, then revert code. Unmount alone keeps atomic indexing active. FTS infrastructure remains until explicitly removed after detach/backup.
compatibility.dependencies: No npm dependencies or new publish files; unchanged 395-file and 6 MiB gates.

boundaries.writerVersions: All writers must use upgraded core before binding registration; old binaries/direct SQL are unsupported. Current-source checks hide stale/deleted content and diagnostics identify drift.
boundaries.recovery: Existing PITR seal explicitly rejects virtual tables. No journaled FTS recovery claim; use consistent SQLite snapshots/rebuilds. Unlinked recovery schemas remain unchanged.
boundaries.administration: Trusted server-only index administration; no automatic browser or MCP mutation exposure.
boundaries.physicalRetention: Byte budget concerns current title/body projection; FTS metadata/pages/WAL and independent backups need operator retention policies.
boundaries.externalRevocation: Rendered data is not proactively erased by external permission changes; dispose/remount on account/workspace changes and discover revocation on subsequent requests.
boundaries.host: Three privileged Docker/XFS skips remain, not certification.

delivery.merge: Expected-head squash through branch protection; no administrative bypass.
